short_description: The umbrella term for every nucleated defence cell in the blood — a mixed GROUP composition (not a single species) showing a lobed-nucleus granulocyte, a round-nucleus lymphocyte and a kidney-bean-nucleus monocyte together among anucleate red blood cells, one of them squeezing through a vessel wall (diapedesis).
composition_note: This is deliberately the GENERIC umbrella entry; the atlas already covers helper T cell, cytotoxic T cell, B cell, natural killer cell, macrophage and neutrophil as their own subjects. Do NOT render a single leukocyte subtype standing in for the whole category — every render must show SEVERAL different white cells together (varying nucleus shape) plus anucleate red cells for contrast, and where the composition allows, one white cell caught mid-diapedesis squeezing between endothelial cells.

labels.en: Red blood cell — anucleate, for contrast

reference.native_size_px: 747x747 (upscaled to 1080x1080 with a plain Lanczos resize by fetch_reference.py — no re-illustration, image is otherwise unmodified)
reference.why_this_one: Genuine Wright/May-Grünwald-Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smear showing TWO different leukocyte types in one frame — a segmented-nucleus granulocyte (neutrophil) and a folded kidney-bean-nucleus monocyte — surrounded by numerous anucleate biconcave red blood cells and a couple of platelets. Exactly the nucleated-vs-anucleate contrast this entry needs. No baked-in text/scale bar/watermark, so no edit_image.py cleaning pass was needed.
